- When sentiment is low (≤0.18) and forecast shows strong upward bias, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 72), model tends to overshoot; cap forecast at +10% above recent peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.  
- If sentiment is high (≥0.53) and forecast is below recent 5-day average, adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to align with bullish sentiment.  
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon; apply 1–3% downward bias for first 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.09–0.18), forecast should be anchored to 10-day moving average rather than 30-day trend.  
- If forecast diverges >5% from true outcome for 3 consecutive days, trigger mean reversion rule: adjust forecast to 20-day weighted average of past 10 days.
